title: Sheafification of a presheaf of rings has as underlying sheaf of sets the sheafification of sets
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme, $T_{\Et}$ its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], $P$ a presheaf of commutative rings (or of rings) on $T_{\Et}$, and $\eta:P\to P^\#$ its sheafification in sheaves of (commutative) rings [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Write $|-|$ for the underlying presheaf of sets. Then $|P^\#|$ is a sheaf of sets and $|\eta|:|P|\to|P^\#|$ is a sheafification of the presheaf of sets $|P|$: every morphism of presheaves of sets from $|P|$ to a sheaf of sets $H$ factors uniquely through $|\eta|$. In particular, for a ring $R$, the constant sheaf of rings $\underline R$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] has as underlying sheaf of sets, with the canonical map from the constant presheaf $U\mapsto R$, the constant sheaf of sets on the underlying set of $R$.

source.place: Section 'Sheaves of algebraic structures' (section-sheaves-algebraic-structures), items (alpha) to (gamma): for a type of algebraic structure (A, s) (rings, with s the underlying set), a presheaf is a sheaf iff its underlying presheaf of sets is, F^# = (F^+)^+ is computed on underlying sets, and sheafification commutes with s (the commutative square (gamma))
